facts.statement: Morrinhosuchus is known from a mandible and the front of a skull found in Monte Alto, São Paulo state, Brazil.
facts.quote: It is known from a mandible and a portion of the front of the skull collected from the municipality of Monte Alto in São Paulo state.

facts.statement: The genus name honors a nearby hill, and the species name honors a chapel located on top of that hill.
facts.quote: Morrinhosuchus refers to Morrinho de Santa Luzia, a hill nearby the collection site of the holotype, while luziae refers to the chapel of Santa Luzia, which is located on top of the hill.

facts.statement: Morrinhosuchus is an extinct notosuchian crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous Adamantina Formation of Brazil.
facts.quote: Morrinhosuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous Adamantina Formation of Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus was described by Iori and Carvalho in 2009.
Morrinhosuchus belongs to the subfamily Caipirasuchinae.
Morrinhosuchus is classified within the family Sphagesauridae.
Morrinhosuchus lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The skull and jaws of Morrinhosuchus are broad at the back but narrow significantly toward the front.
facts.quote: The skull and jaws are posteriorly broad but narrow significantly toward the front.

facts.statement: The mandible of Morrinhosuchus arches upward.
Morrinhosuchus has seven post-caniniform teeth, distinguishing it from Mariliasuchus which has six.
facts.quote: Morrinhosuchus has seven post-caniniform teeth while Mariliasuchus has only six.

facts.statement: Morrinhosuchus likely preyed on Adamantinasuchus, Brasiliguana, and mammals.
facts.quote: Morrinhosuchus may have preyed upon Adamantinasuchus, Brasiliguana and mammals.

facts.statement: Morrinhosuchus was likely prey for predators including Baurusuchus, Campinasuchus, Gondwanasuchus, Pissarrachampsa, Stratiotosuchus, Montealtosuchus, and Pepesuchus.
facts.quote: It was probably eaten by Baurusuchus, Campinasuchus, Gondwanasuchus, Pissarrachampsa, Stratiotosuchus, Montealtosuchus, and Pepesuchus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Morrinhosuchus preyed upon Adamantinasuchus, Brasiliguana, and mammals, as this is a hypothesis based on ecological context.
facts.quote: Morrinhosuchus may have preyed upon Adamantinasuchus, Brasiliguana and mammals.

rejected.quote: The Adamantina Formation, which is Turonian to Santonian in age, was deposited in semi-arid conditions around 95 million years ago.
